chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the missing one from his father? He said: 'Keep it aside until he comes.' I said: 'The man is lost and will not be coming.' So he said: 'If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for the inheritance of a missing heir whose parent has died?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of provisional inheritance distribution, where the missing heir's share is withheld until his return or declared death, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the rights of the absent party. The condition that remaining heirs must be 'trustworthy' (milā’ bi-mālihi) ensures that the set-aside portion is not misappropriated, highlighting the practical application of amanah in estate management. This ruling balances the need for estate liquidity with the certainty of eventual restitution, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh regarding gha'ib.
